title: Government Expands Citizen-Centric Digital Public Service Delivery through UMANG and DigiLocker
body_text:
In line with the Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and empower citizens, the Government of India launched the Digital India programme in July 2015. Under the Digital India programme, the Government has undertaken several initiatives to improve digital access and ensure seamless citizen-centric service delivery including UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) and DigiLocker platforms.
As on 31 st July 2026, approximately 2,575 services [Central Government: 880; State Government: 1695] across India are available on the UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) platform, and 5,437 document types/services [Central Government: 661; State Government: 4,776] are available on DigiLocker platform.
UMANG has more than 11.66 Crore registered users witnessing about 798 Crore transactions in the last 3 years, and DigiLocker has more than 72.43 Crore registered users and has about 72.86 Crore document access transactions in the last 3 years.
The Government has expanded the network of Common Service Centres (CSCs) to improve digital access in rural and remote areas. CSCs provide citizen-centric digital services. These include government, banking, financial, insurance, pension and utility payment services. As on 30 June 2026, 4,07,122 CSCs were functional at the Gram Panchayat level. Of these, 70,069 CSCs were operated by women Village Level Entrepreneurs.
Other key measures to improve digital access and ensure seamless service delivery in rural, remote, and underserved regions are as below:
Mobile and Web-based Access: Both UMANG and DigiLocker platforms are available through mobile applications and web portals, enabling citizens to access Government services anytime and anywhere. Integration with Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): UMANG and DigiLocker is integrated with key Digital Public Infrastructure components such as Aadhaar, eSign, API Setu, and other major digital platforms, enabling seamless and paperless service delivery. Secure and Paperless Governance: Both platforms provide secure authentication, digital document verification and consent-based sharing, reducing the need for physical visits and paper-based processes while ensuring efficient service delivery. Digital Literacy and Awareness: The Government promotes digital literacy through initiatives such as PMGDISHA (Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan) and conducts awareness campaigns to encourage the use of digital platforms. Multilingual and Accessible Services: UMANG and DigiLocker offers services in multiple Indian languages and continuously improves accessibility and user experience to make digital services more inclusive. Continuous Expansion of Services: Government Departments and State Governments are regularly onboarded to integrate more citizen-centric services and digital documents on UMANG and DigiLocker.
This statement was given by the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in Rajya Sabha on 07-08-2026.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Electronics & IT informed Rajya Sabha that as of 31 July 2026, about 2,575 services (880 Central, 1,695 State) are available on UMANG and 5,437 document types/services (661 Central, 4,776 State) on DigiLocker. UMANG has over 11.66 crore registered users with about 798 crore transactions in the last three years, while DigiLocker has over 72.43 crore registered users with about 72.86 crore document access transactions in the last three years. The government also highlighted expansion of Common Service Centres (CSCs), with 4,07,122 functional at the Gram Panchayat level as of 30 June 2026, including 70,069 run by women Village Level Entrepreneurs.
enrichment.context:
UMANG and DigiLocker are flagship platforms under the Digital India programme launched in July 2015, aimed at democratizing access to government services through technology. UMANG serves as a single-window mobile/web app aggregating services across Central and State governments, while DigiLocker enables citizens to store and share verified digital documents, reducing dependence on physical paperwork. Both platforms are integrated with core components of India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) such as Aadhaar, eSign, and API Setu, reflecting India's broader push toward a paperless, API-driven governance model that is increasingly cited internationally as a model for digital public goods.

Common Service Centres (CSCs), operating under the CSC Scheme (part of Digital India), serve as last-mile access points for digital governance in rural and remote areas, run largely by Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). The emphasis on women VLEs ties into broader governance goals of financial and digital inclusion, and gender participation in the digital economy. Complementary literacy initiatives like PMGDISHA (Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan) aim to build digital skills among rural citizens to ensure these platforms are effectively utilized, addressing the digital divide that could otherwise limit the benefits of e-governance to urban, tech-literate populations.

prelims_questions.question: The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) and DigiLocker platforms are initiatives under which of the following programmes?
prelims_questions.explanation: UMANG and DigiLocker were launched as citizen-centric service delivery initiatives under the Digital India programme, which was launched by the Government of India in July 2015.

prelims_questions.question: Common Service Centres (CSCs), which provide last-mile digital governance access in rural India, are primarily operated by whom at the local level?
prelims_questions.explanation: CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level are operated by Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), including a significant number of women VLEs, as highlighted in the release.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) components such as Aadhaar, eSign, and API Setu in enabling seamless and paperless governance in India. Illustrate with reference to platforms like UMANG and DigiLocker.
